title: Adaptive Locomotion Control for Disturbance-Rejecting Quadrupeds
summary: Designed a hybrid model-based and learning-based controller in MuJoCo that recovers from pushes and uneven terrain in real time.
overview: This project combines trajectory optimization with reinforcement learning residuals to improve recovery behaviors in legged locomotion. The full stack was prototyped in simulation before deployment-ready control interfaces were built.
challenge: Purely model-based locomotion degraded under unmodeled contact disturbances.
approach: Built an MPC baseline and augmented it with a learned residual policy trained over randomized terrain and payload shifts.
outcomes: Improved disturbance rejection by 35% over the baseline in randomized tests.
Reduced fall rate during slope transitions from 18% to 6%.
Packaged repeatable benchmark scripts for controller regression testing.

title: ROS2 Fleet Digital Twin for Multi-Robot Coordination
summary: Created a simulation-backed digital twin to test task allocation and collision-aware routing for a heterogeneous mobile manipulator fleet.
overview: A ROS2-native digital twin enabled rapid evaluation of dispatcher policies and failure recovery workflows before field deployment. The environment included realistic latency and sensor-dropout models.
challenge: Hardware-only testing slowed iteration and hid scheduler edge cases.
approach: Implemented a synchronized twin with rosbag replay, fault injection, and planner-in-the-loop evaluation.
outcomes: Cut integration test cycle time from multiple days to a single afternoon.
Identified deadlock scenarios before live rollout.
Improved fleet throughput by 22% with revised allocation heuristics.

title: preCICE-Coupled FSI Model for Soft Gripper Design
summary: Built a preCICE coupling workflow between CFD and structural solvers to evaluate compliance and grasp stability for soft robotic fingers.
overview: The project established a reusable co-simulation pipeline for fluid-structure interaction analysis in soft end-effectors. Parameter sweeps were automated to map geometry-performance tradeoffs.
challenge: Single-physics simulations under-predicted deformation during fast grasp maneuvers.
approach: Linked OpenFOAM and CalculiX through preCICE and integrated optimization scripts for geometry tuning.
outcomes: Established reproducible FSI benchmark cases for gripper design decisions.
Reduced over-compliance failure cases by 28% in simulation.
Documented coupling stability settings for future projects.

title: Vision-Guided Bin Picking with Uncertainty-Aware Grasp Ranking
summary: Trained a grasp scoring model that combines depth imagery and kinematic feasibility checks for robust cluttered bin retrieval.
overview: This effort fused classical grasp candidate generation with uncertainty-calibrated ML ranking. Runtime checks filtered out low-confidence grasp actions before execution.
challenge: Occlusions and reflective surfaces led to high grasp miss rates.
approach: Added uncertainty calibration, active viewpoint updates, and post-grasp verification triggers.
outcomes: Reduced recovery actions and cycle interruptions.
Created a dataset curation tool for failed-grasp replay.

title: Shared-Autonomy Teleoperation for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: Developed a haptic teleoperation stack with assistive autonomy for precision assembly tasks under delayed network conditions.
overview: A shared-autonomy controller blended operator intent with constrained motion planning to reduce errors in narrow-clearance assembly.
challenge: Pure teleop became unstable when delays exceeded 120 ms.
approach: Built predictive intent filters and autonomy handoff logic with tunable authority weighting.
outcomes: Maintained task completion consistency under variable latency.
Published evaluation scripts for controller ablation studies.

title: Model Reduction Pipeline for Fast Soft Robot Simulation
summary: Created a reduced-order modeling workflow that preserves key dynamics for faster controller-in-the-loop experimentation.
overview: The project combined data-driven basis extraction with solver-aware reduction constraints to accelerate closed-loop simulation of compliant systems.
challenge: High-fidelity models were too slow for iterative controller tuning.
approach: Used proper orthogonal decomposition and online correction models to preserve response quality.
outcomes: Achieved 8x faster simulations with acceptable accuracy drift.
Enabled controller sweeps that were previously computationally prohibitive.
Added validation harnesses against full-order references.
